brief: My courtyard is bright indirect with low moisture, and no pets live in the household. A bright but sunless courtyard with fast-draining gravel pots, purely decorative.

design.site_summary: A bright indoor windowsill microclimate for a curious cat with low moisture tolerance requirements.
design.layout_strategy: The scheme is vertically structured with hanging Sedum morganianum trailing from the upper shelf, upright Sedum weinbergii at mid height on the windowsill, and accessible low Haworthia species forming a ground layer at the base.
design.combination_logic: The combination contrasts the long, cascading tendrils of Sedum morganianum with the rosette structure of Sedum weinbergii and the compact, architectural foliage of Haworthia species, creating a rich mix of textures and growth habits year-round.

zones.placement: on the top shelf, 4 h of bright indirect light, sheltered from direct midday sun

plants.why: Provides a wonderful trailing vertical element that fits the bright indirect light of the upper shelf.
plants.role_in_combination: Contributes soft, cascading texture and long green tendrils that contrast sharply with the upright rosette plants below.

maintenance: Water thoroughly only when soil is completely dry every 14 days in summer.
Prune away any damaged stems in spring.

zones.placement: on the windowsill, 5 h of bright indirect morning light, moderate warmth

plants.why: Stands out with its pale rosettes at mid height, thriving in bright indirect windowsill light.
plants.role_in_combination: Adds a distinct color contrast with its silvery-lavender foliage and a robust rosette structure anchoring the middle layer.

maintenance: Water every 10 to 14 days when the potting mix is dry.
Remove lower spent leaves annually in spring.

zones.placement: on the floor edge, easily reachable by cats, 3 h of bright indirect light

plants.why: Safe and low growing, perfect for a pet-accessible ground zone.
plants.role_in_combination: Grounds the composition with dark green, striped textures that invite close inspection by the cat safely.

plants.why: Provides robust, non-toxic textural interest at floor level.
plants.role_in_combination: Complements the standard Haworthia with contrasting white tubercle bands for visual variety.

maintenance: Water every 14 to 21 days depending on ambient humidity.
Wipe leaves gently with a damp cloth monthly to remove dust.

care_instructions.task: Water all succulent zones thoroughly after soil dries out completely.
Reduce watering frequency for all plants during cooler months.
Inspect Sedum morganianum and Haworthia leaves for pest accumulation.

care_cautions: Overwatering the Upper Cascade Zone can cause root rot in Sedum morganianum due to poor drainage in high containers.
The Floor Grazing Zone featuring Haworthia species may experience soil disruption if the cat plays too vigorously with the low rosettes.
design.pet_safety_note: Every plant selected is strictly non-toxic to cats and dogs, and the designated grazing zone ensures safe interaction for your pet.
